**Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F** is a healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] in Denmark. It is actively monitored in the national quality reports for the treatment of [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] (AFDK) published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute. The cluster's performance is evaluated across multiple clinical quality indicators, ranging from anticoagulation treatment coverage to the incidence of stroke and bleeding complications.

In the 2024 AFDK report, Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F was identified as one of the health clusters that failed to meet the national standard of 90% for Indikator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy in newly diagnosed patients, achieving a result of 87.5% [^src1]. Furthermore, the cluster recorded the lowest proportion for [[indikator-4a1|Indikator 4a1]] (1-year treatment coverage) at 85.1% (95% CI: 81.2–88.4) [^src2]. 

The cluster is also tracked for long-term treatment coverage, annual P-creatinine measurements for patients on DOACs, and the incidence of ischemic stroke ([[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]) [^src4]. The national map at the health cluster level shows stroke incidence varying across clusters, placing Nykøbing F in a geographic distribution alongside other entities such as [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] and [[aarhusklyngen|Aarhusklyngen]] [^src4]. Additional monitoring includes severe bleeding within one year of a new diagnosis (Indikator 11), heart failure (Indikator 15) [^src6], mortality (Indikator 9) [^src5], and structured patient education (Indikator 8) [^src8]. In the 2025 report, the cluster continues to be evaluated on indicators such as severe bleeding among prevalent patients [^src9] and mortality [^src11].
